recentItems.title: What no one tells you about freezing your eggs #shorts #tedx
Do not experiment on humans (unless they click accept)  | Christina Giakoumaki | TEDxDeree ACG
recentItems.description:
Are we all just part of a massive, unconsented digital experiment? In this thought-provoking talk, we dive into the dark side of human curiosity and the history of research ethics. From the tragic lessons of the past to the modern reality of "I Accept" buttons, discover how tech platforms are testing on us every day—and why we need to bring human ethics back into the digital age. Dr. Christina Giakoumaki is an Assistant Professor in Communication at Deree–The American College of Greece and Graduate Program Coordinator of the MA in Digital Communication & Social Media. A researcher by training and a rule-examiner by instinct, she has spent over a decade studying how people are persuaded, manipulated, and moved; in advertising, on social media, and increasingly, by artificial intelligence. 
 
Her work has been published in Q1 and Q2 peer-reviewed journals and presented at the American Marketing Association and the British Academy of Management. She holds a PhD in Marketing and Communication from the Athens University of Economics and Business and has served as principal investigator on funded research examining how AI-generated imagery shapes consumer perceptions. 
As a long-standing member and chair of an Academic Integrity Committee and a peer reviewer for over a dozen international journals, Christina has sat on both sides of the boundary line in research. 
Christina is based in Athens, Greece. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 3 rules of adaptability | Spyros Kottoris | TEDxDeree ACG
recentItems.description: In this talk, Spyros Kottoris shares his personal journey through major career pivots and economic collapse to reveal why adaptability is the ultimate skill for navigating an uncertain world. Learn the three rules of adaptability: surfing disruption, finding your core purpose, and recognizing patterns in the chaos. Discover why confidence doesn't come before change, but is what remains after you survive it. Spyros Kottoris is an International Learning & Development Strategist, Sustainability & ESG Expert, and ICF Certified Executive Coach with more than 20 years of international experience designing learning and business transformation solutions across 14 countries and 12 industries. As the founder of Conferia Academy Global, he specializes in leadership development, ESG awareness, business strategy, and people transformation for multinational organizations and senior executives. His work focuses on helping organizations strengthen human-centered skills, leadership culture, and sustainable growth in an AI-driven world. Through his coaching, speaking, and consulting work, he supports leaders and teams in building self-awareness, adaptability, and meaningful impact. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Cum se construiește o moștenire din pierdere | Ciprian Borșan | TEDxCopou
recentItems.description: Ciprian Borșan explorează felul în care pierderile, traumele și crizele pot deveni resurse pentru reconstrucție, atât personală, cât și colectivă. Pornind de la propria experiență și de la vulnerabilitățile societății românești, el vorbește despre creșterea post-traumatică, puterea comunității și nevoia de a transforma durerea în acțiune. Mesajul său ne provoacă să privim altfel momentele dificile: nu doar ca răni pe care le purtăm, ci ca puncte din care putem construi sens, conexiune și o moștenire care rămâne. Ciprian Borșan este antreprenor, specialist în marketing și constructor de comunități, preocupat de impactul pe care mediul de business îl poate avea asupra societății. Este CEO și co-fondator Harpoon Marketing, curator TEDxBaiaMare și președinte fondator al Maramureș Business Club. De asemenea, este președinte RBL Maramureș și membru în Boardul Romanian Business Leaders. Cu experiență în mediul corporatist, antreprenorial și non-profit, Ciprian și-a construit parcursul la intersecția dintre marketing, leadership și dezvoltarea comunităților. Absolvent de Marketing al Universității Babeș-Bolyai din Cluj-Napoca, crede în puterea oamenilor de a genera schimbare atunci când ideile, inițiativa și responsabilitatea față de comunitate se întâlnesc. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Make Room for One More Chair | Jennifer Illich | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if one of the most powerful forms of prevention is helping people feel like they belong?

Through stories from her mother's kitchen table, conversations through FirstLink and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and her own experience with grief, Jennifer Illich explores how human connection shapes our lives. This talk challenges the idea that people need perfect words or solutions and instead highlights the power of creating belonging, staying present, and making room for one more chair.

At its heart, this is a talk about the energy that exists between us and the impact of helping people feel seen, valued, and connected. Jennifer Illich is the Executive Director of FirstLink, a nonprofit organization providing 24/7 crisis support, suicide prevention, and connection to community resources across North Dakota and parts of Minnesota. She has spent more than a decade leading efforts to strengthen how communities respond to people experiencing crisis, including through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and 211 Information and Referral Helpline.
Jennifer believes deeply in the power of human connection and in creating systems where people know they do not have to face their hardest moments alone. Her work brings together crisis services, healthcare, public safety, government, and community partners to improve access to help and build stronger pathways of support.
In 2026, Jennifer was selected as a Bush Fellow, an opportunity she is using to deepen her leadership and explore innovative approaches to crisis care and suicide prevention, particularly for rural, frontier, and underserved communities.
Jennifer holds an MBA from the University of Mary and a bachelor’s degree in Child Development and Family Science from North Dakota State University. At the heart of her work is a simple belief: making room for one more person can change a life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The American Dream needs more owners | Tammy Miller | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
Most Americans spend decades working for companies, yet few ever get the opportunity to own part of one. That simple difference often explains why some workers build lasting wealth while others struggle to get ahead.

In this TEDxFargo talk, Tammy Miller explores the transformative power of employee ownership—a model that gives employees the opportunity to share in the value they help create. Employee ownership may be one of the most scalable and inclusive wealth-building opportunities in America. As the nation faces a historic transfer of business ownership, it presents a rare opportunity to broaden prosperity, preserve local businesses, strengthen communities, and reimagine what it means to achieve the American Dream.
 Tammy J. Miller is a business executive, board leader, and public servant dedicated to helping organizations, communities, and individuals reach their full potential.

Miller previously served as the 39th Lieutenant Governor of North Dakota, where she championed economic development, workforce initiatives, innovation, and policies that strengthened businesses and communities across the state.

Prior to public service, she spent 29 years at Border States, one of the nation's largest 100% employee-owned companies. Beginning as Accounting Manager, she advanced through leadership roles of increasing responsibility. From 2006 to 2020, during her tenure as CEO and Board Chair, she led the company through a period of transformational growth, increasing annual sales from $485 million to nearly $2.5 billion while reinforcing its employee-owned culture and positioning the company for sustained growth.

Today, Miller serves on the board of a publicly traded company. She is a founder and board chair of the North Dakota Center for Employee Ownership, where she advances employee ownership as a proven strategy for business succession, employee wealth creation, and stronger communities. She also coaches business leaders and serves as board chair of the Plains Art Museum.

Miller has received numerous leadership honors, including an Honorary Doctor of Business from Minnesota State University Moorhead in recognition of her contributions to business, public service, and community leadership. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Limitless connectivity: Infinite potential of human connection | Megan Burke Roudebush | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description: This talk covers the possibilities available when people connect the right way. Megan Burke Roudebush, global secure connectivity expert and entrepreneur, highlights how thoughtful questions make the potential of human connection limitless. By pivoting from "no" to something else, Roudebush draws on how her experience as an AP-trained child journalist taught her to ask the right questions at the right time. Megan Burke Roudebush is the Founder and CEO of keepwith®, a relationship technology company built around helping people create meaningful, real-world connections. An attorney, business leader, former Chief Compliance Officer, and lifelong relationship-builder, Megan began her career as a child journalist traveling the world with Children’s Express News Service. After moving to Chicago without knowing anyone, she developed a deliberate approach to networking that grew into a global speaking career—and eventually a company. A 2019 Shark Tank audition became the catalyst for Megan to leave her executive career and build keepwith® full-time, with a focus on making relationship-building more intentional, human, and safe. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Zhong “中” | Qihui Huang | TEDxNew Channel Qingdao
recentItems.description:

TEDx events are independently organized by volunteers. The guidelines we give TEDx organizers are described in more detail here: http://storage.ted.com/tedx/manuals/tedx_content_guidelines.pdf

这位从药香中走出的"中医少女"，16岁蒙眼辨药，全网播放量破6亿。光环之下，她却打破了"成为医生"的唯一标准答案——拍视频做科普，让远方的陌生人因一条留言而受益；背单词学数理，为古老中医寻找年轻化的表达。从诊室到屏幕，从国内到海外，她活出一种不被定义的"中"：不偏执一端，在看似分裂的热爱里找到平衡。 Huang Qihui, born in 2007, is the ninth-generation descendant of Huang Yuanyu, imperial physician to Emperor Qianlong, and a high school student at Jinqiu International Qingdao. Since childhood, she has studied traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) through clinical practice with her parents and under renowned experts including Tang Zuxuan, Li Tiangui, Gao Shuzhong, and Song Zhaopu.

Beyond TCM, she has participated in competitions including AMC12, AIME, ARML, the Australian Mathematics Competition, and the Asian Business Simulation. She also holds a Level-9 certificate in traditional Chinese painting.

As a young ambassador for TCM culture, she shares TCM knowledge through new media, reaching over 778,000 users. At 16, her appearance on The Yellow River Culture Conference generated over 600 million online views. Through media, public speaking, and cross-disciplinary learning, she hopes to inspire young people to rediscover the value of TCM and traditional culture in contemporary life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Healing through two worlds of medicine | Rotshennon:ni Two-Axe | TEDxMcGill
recentItems.description: Medicine and healing are often discussed as universally understood concepts, but they can look vastly different from one perspective to another. In his talk, Rotshennón:ni Two-Axe discusses how healing exists in the space between Western medicine and Indigenous knowledge. Drawing on his work in emergency care and his studies in medicine he describes the intersection between two systems of care: community-rooted Onkwehón:we understandings of health and Western medical practice.  Rotshennon:ni Two-Axe (meaning he is happy), is a second-year medical student at McGill University who is a part of the turtle clan from the Kanien’kehá:ka nation in Kahnawake. Outside of being a medical student at McGill, Rotshennon:ni is a paramedic in his community and is part of a year-long kanien’kéha language program that is land, culture, and healing-based. His talk will bring together two worlds of medicine, the Indigenous and Western understandings of medicine. In Western medicine, illness is often something to be diagnosed and treated; in Indigenous knowledge, healing is about restoring balance between body, mind, spirit, and community. He wants the audience to leave with an understanding of what it truly means to heal, beyond the purely physical state. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Pay attention | Alisha Espey | TEDxDavenport
recentItems.description: What if the people we often underestimate have something essential to teach us about how to live? Through reflections on her relationship with her sister Kara, Alisha Espey explores what attention, ordinary moments and unconditional love can reveal about a meaningful life. In a culture shaped by distraction and striving, this talk invites us to pay attention and reconsider where wisdom lives. Alisha Espey is a storyteller, placemaking professional, and event organizer based in the Quad Cities. A believer in the power of connection and belonging, she leads programs and events for the Downtown Davenport Partnership. Inspired by her relationship with her sister Kara, her TEDx talk explores what people we often underestimate can teach us about attention, joy, and love. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Having a Mortgage Mindset | Zachary Greez | TEDxTASIS England Youth
recentItems.description: In this TEDx talk, Zachary encourages others to move beyond self-imposed limits and predetermined expectations, embracing growth through courage, persistence, and action. His message is simple: success begins when people stop waiting for the perfect moment and start taking the first step. Inspired by Reid Hoffman's quote, “If you aren’t embarrassed by the first version of your product, you shipped too late,” Zachary believes that progress comes from learning, adapting, and having the confidence to begin before everything feels perfect. As the 11th Grade Class President, Zachary is passionate about creating opportunities that empower others to succeed. With interests in finance, mortgages, equitable home buying, and addressing income inequality, he is committed to understanding and tackling the economic challenges that impact communities. Beyond leadership, he is currently involved in developing software for NMBNOW, combining technology and innovation to create meaningful solutions. Through this work and personal experiences, he has developed a strong belief in the power of action and execution. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Conexiunea umană există înaintea limbajului | Mara Crăcăleanu | TEDxIasi
recentItems.description: Filmarea într-una dintre cele mai securizate închisori din Europa, deținuți care oferă espresso și ciocolată unei echipe cu care nu vorbesc aceeași limbă, un bunic convins să se întoarcă într-un loc de care fugise toată viața. Pornind de la copilăria petrecută cu Alice in Wonderland ca refugiu și de la întrebarea unei fetițe de cinci ani, „unde se duc toate cuvintele pe care le spui la radio?", acest talk este despre poveștile care ne apropie și despre curajul de a rămâne curios acolo unde alții își întorc privirea. Pentru că nu împărțim aceleași vieți, dar trăim aceleași povești, iar distanța dintre noi e, de multe ori, mai mică decât credem. Mara Crăcăleanu este una dintre vocile emergente ale industriei cinematografice europene și fondatoarea Melancholia Pictures, companie prin care dezvoltă coproducții internaționale în Europa și America de Nord. Originară din Iași și stabilită la Londra, a fost inclusă la doar 24 de ani în clasamentul Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2026, iar proiectele sale au acumulat peste 70 de selecții și premii internaționale la festivaluri precum BFI Flare, Torino Film Festival și TIFF. Printre cele mai importante momente ale carierei sale se numără premiul Council of Europe Series Co-Production Development Award pentru proiectul „Near Light - Second Lives of Murderers". This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
